'''David Kazhdan''' ({{langx|he|דוד קשדן}}), born '''Dmitry Aleksandrovich Kazhdan''' ({{langx|ru|Дмитрий Александрович Каждан}}; born 20 June 1946), is a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Israel]]i [[mathematician]] known for work in [[representation theory]]. Kazhdan is a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|1990 MacArthur Fellow]]. In 2012, he received the [[Israel Prize]] for Mathematics and Computer sciences.<ref name=":0" />

==Biography==
Kazhdan was born on 20 June 1946 in [[Moscow]], [[USSR]].<ref>{{cite book |title=The MacArthur Fellows Program: the first decade, 1981-1991 |year=1993 |page=180 }}</ref>  His father is [[Alexander Kazhdan]]. He earned a doctorate under [[Alexandre Kirillov]] in 1969 and was a member of [[Israel Gelfand]]'s school of mathematics. He is [[Jewish]], and emigrated from the Soviet Union to take a position at [[Harvard University]] in 1975.  He changed his name from Dmitri Aleksandrovich to David and became an [[Orthodox Jew]] around that time.

In 2002, he immigrated to Israel and is now a professor at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] as well as a [[Professors in the United States#Professor emeritus and emerita|professor emeritus]] at Harvard.

On October 6, 2013, Kazhdan was critically injured in a car accident while riding a bicycle in Jerusalem.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/National-News/Israel-Prize-winner-in-serious-condition-following-hit-and-run-in-Jerusalem-328080|title=Israel Prize winner in serious condition following hit-and-run in Jerusalem|newspaper=The Jerusalem Post &#124; Jpost.com }}</ref>

Kazhdan has four children.  His son, [[Eli Kazhdan]], was general director of [[Natan Sharansky]]'s [[Yisrael BaAliyah]] political party (now merged with [[Likud]]), chief of staff in the [[Ministry of Economy (Israel)|Ministry of Industry and Trade]] and the [[Ministry of Interior (Israel)|Ministry of Interior]], and a foreign policy advisor to Sharansky.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kazhdan |first=Eli |title=What Exactly Does Israel Have on Yasser Arafat? |website=[[Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs]] |date=September 30, 2003 |accessdate=2025-11-30 |url=https://jcfa.org/article/what-exactly-does-israel-have-on-yasser-arafat/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251130120911/https://jcfa.org/article/what-exactly-does-israel-have-on-yasser-arafat/ |archive-date=2025-11-30 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Research==
He is known for collaboration with [[Israel Gelfand]], [[Victor Kac]], [[George Lusztig]] (on the [[Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture]] on [[Verma module]]s), with [[Grigory Margulis]] ([[Kazhdan–Margulis theorem]]), with [[Yuval Flicker]] and [[S. J. Patterson]] on the representations of [[metaplectic group]]s. [[Kazhdan's property (T)]] is widely used in representation theory.

Kazhdan held a [[MacArthur Fellowship]] from 1990 to 1995.  He was the doctoral advisor of [[Vladimir Voevodsky]], a recipient of the [[Fields Medal]], one of the highest awards in mathematics. Kazhdan has been a member of [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] since 1990,  of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Israel Academy of Sciences]] since 2006, and of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 2008.  In 2012, he was awarded the [[Israel Prize]], the country's  highest academic honor, for mathematics and computer science.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://support.huji.ac.il/news-events/news/kazhdan_award_mathematics2012/ |title=Israel Prize for mathematics and computer science for 2012 to Prof. David Kazhdan |access-date=2012-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053850/http://support.huji.ac.il/news-events/news/kazhdan_award_mathematics2012/ |archive-date=2013-09-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2020 he received the [[Shaw Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref>[https://www.shawprize.org/prizes/mathematical-sciences Shaw Prize 2020]</ref>
